generic_name: Sodium Sulfate, Potassium Sulfate, and Magnesium Sulfate
purpose: This medication is used to clean out your colon (large intestine) before a colonoscopy or other bowel procedure. It works by flushing out all the stool from your intestines so your doctor can get a clear view. A clean colon helps your doctor spot any problems like polyps or signs of cancer.
how_it_works: This medicine draws water into your intestines, which softens and loosens stool. This causes your bowels to empty completely, almost like a strong cleanse. Think of it as a powerful flush that clears everything out so your colon is nice and clean for the procedure.
common_side_effects: You will likely have a lot of diarrhea — that is expected and is how the medicine is supposed to work. You may also feel bloated, have stomach cramps, nausea, or vomiting. Some people feel dizzy or lightheaded due to fluid loss.
warnings: It is very important to drink plenty of clear liquids to avoid dehydration. If you have kidney problems, heart problems, or are on certain blood pressure or water pills (diuretics), let your doctor know before using this. Do not take it within 1 hour of other medications, as it can prevent them from being absorbed properly. Stop and call your doctor if you have severe stomach pain or no bowel movement after taking it.
typical_dosing: Usually taken in two doses — one the evening before your procedure and one the morning of your procedure. Each dose is mixed with water and must be followed by drinking additional clear fluids. Follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions exactly, as timing is very important for a successful bowel prep.
